title: Early Impact & Probation — 45d Activation Accelerator
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for manager + people ops to run a focused 45-day probation / early-impact activation for new hires (IC and manager lanes). It combines a prioritized task list, an early-eval scoring rubric, sample interview touchpoints for hiring validation, and a lightweight hiring prioritization matrix when backfilling roles mid-quarter.

Audience:
- Hiring manager (primary)
- People Ops partner (co-owner)
- HRBP and recruiting for any escalations

High-level goals (what success looks like at day 45):
- New hire has 2 ship-ready contributions (PRs, documentation pages, customer-runbook items) or one player-owned small project with clear metrics.
- Manager has recorded 2 check-ins (week 1 & week 3) with measurable signals against the rubric.
- Ramp blockers are surfaced and a 30-day remediation plan is committed if needed.
- Candidate rating retained for future hiring intelligence (pass / conditional / fail).

Quick operating principles (people-ops lens):
- Keep check-ins short, consistent cadence. Week 1 = 30 min, Week 3 = 45 min, Week 6 = 60 min.
- Make expectations explicit at hire: share this playbook in offer packet (one pager).
- Collect asynchronous evidence: PR links, meeting notes, customer feedback, product telemetry.

45-day timeline (practical schedule):
Week 0 (offer → day 1):
- Send Welcome packet + 45d one-pager (this doc condensed).
- Manager creates 45d onboarding card in Jira/Notion.
- Assign buddy and first deliverable (small scaffolded task).

Week 1 (1–7):
- Day 1: 30m orientation call + team intro.
- Days 2–5: focus on infra access, local dev loop, first ticket.
- End-of-week: Week1 check-in (30m) — manager fills quick rubric.

Week 2–3 (8–21):
- Incremental task ownership. Shadow cross-functional calls once.
- Week3: working demo or PR. Manager does mid-probation 45m check-in; collect peer feedback (2 peers).

Week 4–5 (22–35):
- Ownership increases. Start a small project slice that can be shipped by day 45.
- People Ops runs optional 1:1 to collect early sentiment if flagged.

Week 6–7 (36–45):
- Finalize deliverable, write handover notes, prepare 45d summary.
- Day 45: Formal probation review meeting (60m) + outcome recorded.

Manager checklist (practical items):
- Before day 1: create first tickets, add to team calendar, confirm buddy.
- Day 1: share 45d expectations doc, confirm access matrix.
- Weekly: update evidence log (PRs, notes).
- Solicit 2 peer signals by week 3.
- Schedule and prepare for day 45 review (include HR/People Ops).

Evidence log (minimal required artifacts):
- Link to first PR/issue with reviewer comments.
- Short demo recording or Miro screenshot of work.
- Two peer quick-feedback blurbs (1–2 sentences each).
- Owner-written 45d reflection (what went well, blockers, next priorities).

Lightweight early-eval rubric (use numeric scores 1–5 and short notes):
- Technical delivery (1–5): implements small tasks, code quality, reviewer feedback handled.
- Communication & collaboration (1–5): clear updates, syncs, peer work.
- Product judgment / prioritization (1–5): picks sensible scope, asks clarifying questions.
- Reliability & autonomy (1–5): meets commitments, follows up, escalates appropriately.
- Impact potential (1–5): signs of multiplier effects or strong learning curve.

Scoring guidance:
- Pass: aggregate >= 16 with no single category <= 2 and manager recommends continuation.
- Conditional: aggregate 12–15 OR any category == 2 — create 30d remediation (specific success criteria).
- Fail: aggregate < 12 OR any category == 1 — escalate to People Ops for next steps.

Sample peer feedback template (keeps responses short):
- Role/relationship: (peer engineer, product manager)
- Observed behavior in last 2 weeks: (2–3 sentences)
- Strengths: (1–2 bullets)
- Areas to watch/help: (1 bullet)

Hiring prioritization matrix (mini decision aid for backfills):
Columns: Impact (1–5), Time-to-fill risk (1–5), Ramp time (1–5), Cross-team dependency (1–5).
Scoring heuristic: Priority score = Impact * (6 - Time-to-fill) — qualitative override if dependency==5.
Usage note: recruiting and hiring manager fill matrix together to decide reorder of reqs. Keep evidence in JIRA card.

Sample interview touchpoints for late-stage hires (to validate probation signals early):
- Recruiter screen: focus on culture fit and logistics (done).
- Hiring manager call: share concrete expectations (include 45d outcomes).
- Technical assignment: aim for scoped micro-project that mirrors first ticket. Use same rubric when grading.
- Panel: include future peer(s) who will write week3 signals.

9 common blockers and mitigations (notes to self):
- Access gaps: escalate to infra on day 1 and copy People Ops.
- Unclear scope: break tasks into 1–2 day check-ins.
- Over-mentoring: nudge to pair less; encourage independent PR ownership.
- Remote timezone lag: set overlap hours for 2–3 core hours.
- People dynamics mismatch: collect early peer notes and run a mediator sync before day 30.

Template: 45d review summary (fill during day 45 meeting):
- Role & hire date:
- Manager:
- Summary of deliverables:
- Rubric scores + short rationale per category:
- Peer notes (2):
- Outcome recommendation: pass / conditional (with remediation) / fail
- Next steps and owner(s):

Open questions / follow ups (working):
- Should we standardize the scoring thresholds across teams? (pros/cons).
- Pilot adding a customer feedback channel for client-facing hires (UX/CS).
- Determine if 45d should be mandatory for ICs under L2 vs managers — drafting policy.

Notes to people-ops reviewer:
- This is a living doc: prefer short, scannable templates so managers actually use it.
- We should ship a 1-page version to attach to offer emails.
- Recruiters should reference the micro-assignment alignment with week 1 ticket.

Appendix — quick copy for offer email (one paragraph):
"At Redwood, we run a focused 45-day activation to help new team members ramp quickly and get meaningful work out the door. You’ll be assigned a first deliverable, a buddy, and a manager who will run two short check-ins. Outcomes are evaluated on a simple rubric — most hires pass; where help is needed we agree a remediation plan. We share this to set clear expectations."
